evidence: Scenario routine-induction carries stable content version 0.1.0.
Capability version 0.1.0-alpha.48 is bound by this audit.
The declarative scenario schema validates a bounded fictional patient profile.
5 objectives map to debrief rubric evidence.

routine-induction-fixtures.ts binds seed 4207 and content 0.1.0 to expert, wrong-clock error, one-decision recovery, and no-action paths over 5,400 ticks. Unlike the module lessons, nothing here is an authored constant: the forty-two-year-old woman of 68 kg is a set of baseline parameters and everything the transcripts are scored on — seconds at an end-tidal oxygen fraction of 0.9, seconds of mean arterial pressure below 65, the lowest saturation, the percentage the heart rate rose after incision — is computed by the compartment solver and the haemodynamic model from published pharmacology. No outcome is authored and none follows from any choice. tests/integration/anesthesia-routine-induction-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.
The timeline contains at least one non-narrative state event.

This lesson has no tray of its own and no lesson-specific action. It drives the ordinary cockpit — the flowmeter, a propofol syringe, a remifentanil syringe, a laryngoscope and the ventilator — and every one of those is available from the first tick in any order. What separates the transcripts is not which controls were reachable but when they were used against a patient who was changing while the learner decided. The expert path is five actions; the error path is the same five with one more, given six seconds after the induction dose against a hundred-second time to peak. The lesson intubates nobody, gives no real drug, and predicts no outcome for any person.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The transcripts end at 5,400 ticks, which is nine simulated minutes: past incision at tick 3,600 and past port insertion at 4,800, so the two stimulus events the timeline declares have both been answered. There is no emergence, no extubation and no end of operation in this scenario, and the briefing does not offer one. The run stops because the slice it models is over, not because the patient reached a state.

Nine authored tutor rules at version 0.1.0 in tutor/guidance.ts cover four of the five objectives as a ladder rather than a single prompt per state: orient, notice, connect, prioritize, direct and explain for preoxygenation, then one each for ventilation, the effect-site wait, and treating the mechanism of the pressure fall. They carry cooldowns and an urgency flag, so coached withholds everything that is not about to hurt the patient and unassisted says nothing at all while unpromptedOmissions still records what went unsaid for the debrief. No rule covers blunt-incision, and this evidence does not claim one. Worked example 0.2.0 is the flagship demonstration linked from the landing page, driving the ordinary controls through the real engine and the real models. Its induction beats moved from 190/195 s to 230/235 s at this version, because at the earlier timing the example secured the airway with 150 seconds of end-tidal reserve and scored partly met on the preoxygenation objective it exists to teach; it now measures 190.6 seconds and the beat at 220 s names both clocks out loud. tests/unit/demonstration.test.ts asserts every narration promise against the engine, including that wait, and tests/integration/anesthesia-routine-induction-runs.test.ts pins the transcripts and the version binding.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx derives all five objectives from the replayed state trace rather than from a score kept during the run. The counterfactual is the clock. The objective says "End-tidal, not inspired", and in this patient the end-tidal fraction does not reach 0.9 until about 97 seconds after the flowmeter moves — so an induction three minutes after turning the oxygen up arrives with roughly 150 seconds of reserve against an objective that asks for 180. The error and recovery paths share that opening exactly and differ in one decision: whether a second propofol dose is given while the first is still climbing. Measured, that single difference moves hysteresis from not met to met and takes the pressure nadir from 56.4 to 62.3 mmHg. Neither path recovers the preoxygenation deficit, because seconds already spent cannot be recovered, and the evidence says so rather than offering a path that pretends otherwise.
3 source citation(s) are declared.
5 limitation record(s) are linked.

routine-induction-fixtures.ts binds exact-content expert, wrong-clock error, one-decision recovery, and no-action pathways to seed 4207 for deterministic replay through the shared engine. Scored through the real debrief, the expert path meets all five objectives; the error path is partly met, not met, partly met, met, met; the recovery path is partly met, met, partly met, met, met; and the no-action path is not met, met, met, met, partly met. The expert path carries no vasopressor, because one was measured and changes the pressure nadir by less than a tenth of a millimetre of mercury in this patient — a reference transcript should not contain an action that does nothing.
Automated UI, observed-state and replay checks exist. Exact-version assistive-technology, keyboard, phone, zoom, reduced-motion, offline, and performance validation remains pending.
The scenario inherits the shared report control and has an exact-version Worker catalog record. Complete four-surface runtime evidence is not yet bound.

scenarios.title: Rapid desaturation in the obese patient

evidence: Scenario rapid-desaturation carries stable content version 0.1.0.
Capability version 0.1.0-alpha.48 is bound by this audit.
The declarative scenario schema validates a bounded fictional patient profile.
4 objectives map to debrief rubric evidence.

rapid-desaturation-fixtures.ts binds seed 5310 and content 0.1.0 to expert, no-preoxygenation error, same-haste recovery, and no-action paths over 5,400 ticks. Nothing the objectives are scored on is authored: the fifty-four-year-old man of 138 kg is a set of baseline parameters and an obese respiratory profile, and the saturation, the end-tidal oxygen fraction, the laryngoscopic grade and the number of attempts all come out of the shared engine. The airway is genuinely stochastic — at this seed the first direct attempt returns a Cormack-Lehane grade 3 view and fails, and the second places the tube — which is why the transcripts record what the engine did rather than asserting a result. tests/integration/anesthesia-rapid-desaturation-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.
The timeline contains at least one non-narrative state event.

No tray of its own and no lesson-specific action: the flowmeter, two syringes, a laryngoscope with a choice of technique, and the ventilator, all available from the first tick. Two choices carry the lesson. The first is the propofol dose: the formulary offers a 2 mg/kg preset that gives 276 mg on this patient's total body weight, and the transcripts use the fixed 160 mg that is roughly 2 mg/kg of lean body mass instead — the scenario's own formulary comment says a 50 mL syringe was drawn up precisely so that the syringe would not make that decision for the learner. The second is the technique: the airway assessment names a Mallampati III view, 5.5 cm thyromental distance, limited neck extension and a beard before anything is given, and the expert path reaches for video first because of it. The lesson intubates nobody, gives no real drug, and predicts no outcome for any person.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The transcripts end at 5,400 ticks with the airway secured and the ventilator delivering. There is no maintenance, emergence or end of operation in this scenario and the briefing does not offer one: the slice is induction and the airway, and the run stops because that slice is over rather than because the patient reached a state.

The nine authored tutor rules at version 0.1.0 in tutor/guidance.ts apply here, and the two that matter most in this patient are the preoxygenation ladder and the apnoea-after-bolus prompt: they read inspired oxygen, the recorded boluses and state the engine produced anyway, so unassisted is silent and coached withholds everything that is not about to hurt him. Worked example 0.1.0 is the anaesthesia module's first, and it is built differently from every other worked example in the catalog. The module lessons read an assessment sidecar where each step is a tick that is either null or not; this lesson has none, so every beat is gated on a physiological quantity or on a drug that has arrived in the plasma — the flowmeter setting, the end-tidal fraction, the engine's own preoxygenation counter, whether he is still breathing, and the airway. Reading the plasma rather than an action list is what makes it resumable: a learner can take the controls, do something, and hand them back, and the example picks up from the patient rather than from a script. Several of its beats dispatch nothing at all, which is the point — the two waiting beats are the ones a learner is tempted to skip, and an example that fast-forwarded through them would teach exactly what this patient exists to punish. The airway beats repeat as many times as the airway needs, because the view is drawn from a distribution rather than scripted: at this seed the first video attempt does not place the tube and the second does, and an example that could only show a first attempt working would be scripted after all. No beat turns the ventilator on, because the engine starts delivering when the tube is placed and a beat that dispatched it would be unreachable. The flagship scripted demonstration is NOT this: that is authored against routine induction, its seed and its patient, and the route offers it by scenario id through a separate branch. tests/unit/anesthesia-rapid-desaturation-worked-example.test.ts drives every beat through the real engine to a secured airway, and tests/unit/worked-example-offer.test.ts pins that what this audit claims is what the product actually offers.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx derives all four objectives from the replayed state trace and the engine event log rather than from a score kept during the run. The counterfactual is the previous lesson. Routine induction teaches that preoxygenation buys time; this patient exists to say what that time is worth, and the error path finds out by treating him like the healthy forty-two-year-old — no oxygen, induce, take the airway. Measured, the saturation reaches 54.5%, and that number is produced by the obese profile's smaller functional residual capacity and higher oxygen consumption rather than authored. The recovery path carries the same impatience, inducing with 94 seconds of end-tidal reserve so the preoxygenation objective is partly met and stays that way, but the oxygen was running and the airway is taken promptly: the saturation never leaves its room-air baseline of 93.8%. Same haste, different margin.

rapid-desaturation-fixtures.ts binds exact-content expert, no-preoxygenation error, same-haste recovery, and no-action pathways to seed 5310 for deterministic replay through the shared engine. Scored through the real debrief, the expert path meets all four; the error path is not met, not met, met, met; the recovery path is partly met, met, met, met; and the no-action path is not met, met, not exercised, met. The limit-attempts objective is met on every path that reaches an airway and is not failed by any of them, which is a property of the case rather than of the transcripts: the engine has never needed more than two accepted direct attempts on this patient across the seeds tested, and a transcript that failed it would have to be built to fail. This evidence claims the objective is exercised, not that it is stressed.
